reminders.title: Eye break
reminders.body: Look away from the screen and focus on a distant object for 20 seconds. Blink slowly and let your eyes relax.
instruction_steps: Turn your gaze from the screen to something about 6 m (20 ft) away.
Keep looking for 20 seconds and blink normally before returning.
reminders.safety_note: This is general visual hygiene guidance, not medical advice. Persistent eye symptoms should be assessed by an eye-care professional.
reminders.visual_description: A worker looks away from the nearby monitor toward a distant outdoor point.

reminders.title: Posture reset
reminders.body: Relax your shoulders. Keep your head level, wrists straight, elbows close, and both feet fully supported.
instruction_steps: Support both feet on the floor or a footrest.
Let your shoulders drop and keep your head level.
Bring your elbows close and return with straight, relaxed wrists.
reminders.safety_note: Do not force a position that causes pain. Adjust workstation equipment where possible.
reminders.visual_description: A worker sits with a level head, supported back, straight wrists, and supported feet.

reminders.title: Move for a minute
reminders.body: Stand up, walk gently, and loosen your hips and back before returning to work.
instruction_steps: Stand only when the area and current task are safe.
Walk at an easy pace and let your arms move naturally.
Return to work in a comfortable, supported position.
reminders.safety_note: Move within your safe range and workplace rules.
reminders.visual_description: A worker walks gently away from the workstation for a short movement break.

reminders.title: Neck and shoulder release
reminders.body: Let your arms rest at your sides. Gently roll your shoulders back, then bring your head back to a comfortable neutral position.
instruction_steps: Sit or stand tall with your head facing forward.
Roll both shoulders slowly backward five times.
Repeat forward, then let your shoulders settle.
reminders.safety_note: Keep the movement gentle. Stop if you feel dizziness, tingling, sharp pain, or worsening symptoms.
reminders.visual_description: A worker keeps the head neutral while gently rolling relaxed shoulders backward.

reminders.title: Hands and wrists reset
reminders.body: Take your hands off the keyboard or mouse. Open and close your hands slowly, then return with wrists straight and relaxed.
instruction_steps: Lift both hands away from the keyboard or mouse.
Open the fingers, then make a loose fist with each thumb outside.
Open again without forcing the fingers and repeat slowly.
reminders.safety_note: Avoid forceful stretching. Persistent numbness, weakness, or pain should be checked by a qualified clinician.
reminders.visual_description: A worker lifts both hands from the keyboard and gently opens the fingers with straight wrists.

reminders.title: Voice and breathing reset
reminders.body: Pause between calls when possible. Relax your jaw, lower your shoulders, and take two slow nasal breaths before the next task.
instruction_steps: Pause only when there is no active call or urgent task.
Unclench your jaw and let your shoulders lower.
Take two comfortable breaths through your nose.
reminders.safety_note: This is a general comfort prompt. Follow your workplace procedures and seek professional care for persistent voice or breathing symptoms.
reminders.visual_description: A call-center worker relaxes the jaw and shoulders while taking a slow nasal breath.

reminders.title: Control-room posture scan
reminders.body: Before the next monitoring cycle, check that your screens are easy to view, your shoulders are relaxed, and your feet are supported.
instruction_steps: Keep all safety-critical displays in view.
Check that your head faces forward and your shoulders are relaxed.
Support both feet and bring frequently used controls within easy reach.
reminders.safety_note: Do not interrupt safety-critical monitoring. Use this prompt only when operationally safe.
reminders.visual_description: A control-room operator maintains neutral posture while continuing to monitor three screens.

reminders.title: Parked mobility break
reminders.body: When parked safely, step out if permitted, walk briefly, and move your ankles, hips, and shoulders before driving again.
instruction_steps: Park securely in a permitted place and finish the driving task.
Step out only when site and traffic conditions are safe.
Walk gently, then settle into a comfortable position before restarting.
reminders.safety_note: Never do this while driving. Follow road, site, and employer safety rules.
reminders.visual_description: A driver walks gently beside a vehicle that is safely parked in a marked space.

reminders.title: Shoulder shrug and release
reminders.body: Gently raise both shoulders, pause briefly, then let them relax to interrupt a fixed shoulder position.
instruction_steps: Sit or stand tall with your arms loose and head level.
Raise both shoulders toward your ears only to slight tension.
Hold briefly, then release fully and repeat.
reminders.safety_note: Use no weights and do not force the lift. Stop for pain, tingling, numbness, or dizziness.
reminders.visual_description: A guide slowly raises both shoulders, pauses, and releases them to neutral.

reminders.title: Gentle overhead reach
reminders.body: Reach upward through a comfortable range to change your upper-body position after desk work.
instruction_steps: Stand steadily with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Loosely interlace your fingers and reach upward without arching your back.
Breathe normally, lower your arms slowly, and repeat once.
reminders.safety_note: Keep the range comfortable and joints unlocked. Skip this movement if overhead reach is restricted or painful.
reminders.visual_description: A standing start pose transitions to a comfortable two-arm overhead reach with an upward arrow.

reminders.title: Seated side reach
reminders.body: Use a small side reach to change position while keeping your seat and feet supported.
instruction_steps: Use a stable chair without wheels and place both feet flat.
Raise one arm and lean a small amount to the opposite side.
Keep both sitting bones down, return slowly, and change sides.
reminders.safety_note: Do not pull on the chair or bend deeply. Skip this seated version if the chair can roll or the movement causes pain.
reminders.visual_description: A seated guide raises one arm, makes a small side reach, and returns upright on a stable chair.

reminders.title: Gentle seated turn
reminders.body: Turn your upper body within a comfortable range while keeping your hips and feet facing forward.
instruction_steps: Sit upright on a stable chair with both feet flat.
Keep your hips forward and make a small upper-body turn.
Do not pull with your hands; return to center and change sides.
reminders.safety_note: Keep the movement slow and comfortable. Stop for pain, dizziness, tingling, or worsening symptoms.
reminders.visual_description: Two seated poses show a forward start and a small upper-body turn with hips and feet supported.

reminders.title: Seated chest opener
reminders.body: Sit tall, draw your shoulders back and down, and open your arms gently to change a closed desk posture.
instruction_steps: Use a stable chair without wheels and place both feet flat.
Sit upright, lower your shoulders, and open both arms below shoulder height.
Lift your chest only slightly, breathe normally, then return with control.
reminders.safety_note: Do not force your arms back or arch your lower back. Skip the movement if it is restricted or painful.
reminders.visual_description: A seated guide opens both arms below shoulder height, gently lifts the chest, and returns to neutral.

reminders.title: Seated ankle flex and point
reminders.body: Straighten one leg comfortably and alternate pointing the toes away and drawing them back toward the shin.
instruction_steps: Sit upright on a stable chair and keep one foot flat.
Straighten the other leg a short distance without locking the knee.
Point and flex the ankle slowly, lower the foot, and change sides.
reminders.safety_note: Keep the range comfortable. Drivers must be safely parked with the driving task finished. Stop for pain, numbness, or dizziness.
reminders.visual_description: A seated guide extends one leg and slowly alternates the foot between pointing away and flexing back.

reminders.title: Controlled sit to stand
reminders.body: Use one slow sit-to-stand cycle to change position and move your legs after seated work.
instruction_steps: Use a solid chair without wheels, place your feet hip-width apart, and sit near the front half.
Lean forward slightly from the hips and stand using your legs while looking ahead.
Stand tall, then lower yourself back to the chair slowly and with control.
reminders.safety_note: Make sure the chair cannot slide and the area is clear. Use your hands for guidance or skip the movement if standing without support is not comfortable.
reminders.visual_description: A guide leans forward from a stable chair, stands using the legs, and sits down slowly.

reminders.title: Supported calf raise
reminders.body: Use a stable chair for balance and raise both heels slowly before lowering them with control.
instruction_steps: Stand behind a stable chair with both feet parallel and hip-width apart.
Rest both hands lightly on the chair and raise both heels only as far as comfortable.
Pause briefly, lower both heels slowly, and keep your body upright.
reminders.safety_note: Keep both hands supported and do not use a chair that can roll or slide. Stop for pain, loss of balance, or dizziness.
reminders.visual_description: A standing guide holds a stable chair, raises both heels together, pauses, and lowers them.
